summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for later Q&A)

## BOOK 1: "The Case of the Black Twenty-Two" by Brian Flynn (1929)

### Chapters I-III: Setup, the Galleries
- **Peter Daventry**, junior partner of "Merryweather, Linnell and Daventry, Solicitors" (Cornhill). Hungover after Oxford reunion dinner. Clerk **Plunkett** (35 yrs service). Senior partner **David Linnell** (58, Lancashire-born).
- Client **Laurence P. Stewart**, American millionaire (Chicago/Wall St), widower, one son (~22), bought **Assynton Lodge** near Wantage, Berkshire; collector obsessed with Mary Queen of Scots relics; claims descent from her.
- Letter (June 7th, 192-) from Assynton Lodge asks firm to buy at sale of **Day, Forshaw and Palmers**, Hanover Galleries, W.1 (Fri June 10, 1 o'clock; Lord Clavering's collection). Items: **No. 37 "Collar of Pearls"**, **No. 38 "Antique Tapestry Fire-screen"**, **No. 39 "Rosary of Amber Beads"**. No price limit.
- Peter lunches at **the Violette** (Oxford St; waiter Gustave; Dry Martini; thick white soup, Sole au Colbert, Roast Duck). Friend **Marriott**. Couple at next table (man and woman). Peter says "So's Mary, Queen of Scots!" after Marriott says "Queen Anne's dead"; man knocks cruet to floor. Woman says "let's go to-morrow—not to-day."
- At Galleries Peter inspects items; two plain-clothes men watching. Young **Ronald Forshaw** shows items. Screen: beaded words "JESUS CHRIST, GOD AND SAVIOUR", Scots lion top-left, fleur-de-lis top-right, English leopards/lilies bottom corners. Peter asks how many saw items: "nobody."
- Linnell suspects forgery; telegrams from "Stewart": "Say! What the hell's biting you—when I say Buy—then Buy." and "Same name as before."
- Next morning Mason (night-watchman) murdered; three items stolen. Linnell goes to Galleries; Detective-Inspector **Goodall** (stout, clean-shaven, blue serge). Watchman **Druce** (~60, wizened; 6 yrs service): Mason knocked three times; a woman asked way to Marble Arch and the Galleries opening time; she sneezed walking away. Night-watch relief at midnight; Mrs. Turner the cleaner raised alarm. Mason's office door left unlocked. Owner **Mr. Day** (tall).
- Peter phoned Linnell: Stewart murdered in library at Assynton, skull battered.

### Chapters IV-V: Bathurst, Assynton
- Young Stewart phoned firm (secretary **Llewellyn**, "Morgan"). Peter seeks **Anthony Bathurst** via brother **Gerald Daventry** (M.C.C., Leyton cricket; Bathurst at **Princes** squash club). Bathurst: solved Considine Manor case; free-lance.
- Train 6:55 from Paddington with Goodall too (Goodall, Bathurst, Peter). Bathurst's revolver advice.
- Assynton: **Sergeant Clegg** (Berrington-area local; wife married 17 yrs). Stewart library: French doors bolted, key inside lock. Body at desk, revolver in LEFT dressing-gown pocket, one chamber fired. Note: "Urgent in the morning! M. L." Butler **Butterworth** (60+, ex-Sir Julian Kennedy's, Washington; wife housekeeper, married 37 yrs). Maids Barton, Regan, Evans, Winter; cook Mrs Briggs; gardener Maidment; boot-boy **Patrick O'Connor** (18). Ward **Marjorie Lennox** (petite, retroussé nose, blue eyes). Clegg finds lace handkerchief "M. L." in curtains.
- Marjorie accuses Llewellyn ("he's in the house now"), then storms out. Stewart's son is **Charles Stewart**.

### Chapters VI-IX: Train, Hotel, Night
- Butterworth heard Stewart & a woman's voice ~10:10 in library.
- Train: Goodall, Bathurst, Peter; Bathurst explains "Timeo"? (no—Bathurst reasons on motive). Goodall: "Sergeant Amos Clegg" referred.
- Bathurst's room; at 1:22 a.m. hears steps; sees Llewellyn enter room next but one.

### Chapters X-XIII: Bicycle, Circle, Colonel
- O'Connor's father **Michael O'Connor** (foundry, black beard, 6'2"): bicycle tires marked with fresh tar from road-works; bicycle kept in Maidment's potting-shed; used night of murder.
- Coal scuttle yields mud pellets and four brown stones; ink-bowl has stone. Bathurst theorizes murderer went to Assynton's telephone (Assynton village) to call an hotel; "with a given center, describe a circle" (Hanover Galleries center).
- Clegg: trunk call 11 minutes to **Blanchard's Hotel, Clifford Street** (guest "Mr & Mrs Laurence Charles Stewart" from New York).
- **Colonel Leach-Fletcher** (Neuve Chapelle bungalow; 5'10", 14 st; Bentley): says Stewart worried about treachery; planned interview with son after Colonel left (~10). Stewart had book Renan's "Vie de Jésus" on desk.

### Chapters XIV-XVIII: Letter, Bullet, Memoirs
- Llewellyn's love-letter to Marjorie (hidden in book) threatens; Marjorie showed Laurence it. Bathurst deduces. Piece of jagged stone (magnum-bottle shape) retrieved from pool by Peter barefoot.
- Shot test: Bathurst's shot in Stewart's room (both 'five minutes' shots).
- Bullet found in "Memoirs of Réné de St. Maure—one-time Page to Mary Stuart" (848 pages). Passage: "the Black Twenty-Two"; "Cardinal's great gift"; Thibaut Girardier made two screens (tapestry and beaten metal).
- Blanchard's Hotel: proprietor Blanchard; room 54; sign "Asthma" powder? (fragments); chambermaid Rabjohns (odor of burning); porter Atkins (Mrs Stewart wore black glasses, "my father"). Bathurst discovers hay-fever clue.

### Chapters XIX-XXV: Arrests
- Ricardo's supper; Goodall. Telegram: "M. S." Personal ad ("Both well") = Bothwell at Blanchard's; New York police: **Snoop Mortimer** (alias Flash Alf) & wife **Alice Mortimer** (née Butterworth, Butterworth's daughter).
- Mr Ferguson of Crake and Ferguson (New York) — will: £250,000 to Marjorie & residue to Charles, conditional on marrying each other.
- Carl... Bathurst orders Charles to close house. Night raid at Assynton Lodge: Butterworth, Mortimer, Alice arrested. Screens: tapestry screen hollow fish with 22 black pearls of Lorraine. Greek "ICHTHUS" anagram: "Ιησοῦς Χριστός Θεός Σωτήρ"; "Timeo Danaos".
- Conclusion: Butterworth killed Stewart; Stewart's dressing-gown revolver; Charles and Marjorie's future; Bathurst marries? (Charles will marry Rosemary Armitage per Charles; Marjorie to Llewellyn? Not stated).

---

## BOOK 2: "The Slave of Silence" by F. M. White (1906)

### Chapters I-II: Dinner eve
- **Beatrice Darryll** (22, dark dress, blue eyes, warm hair), daughter of **Sir Charles Darryll** (boyish, debts, City company fraud). Wedding next day (to **Stephen Richford**, heavy man, thick lip, millionaire, bullying) at Royal Palace Hotel. Watchers outside.
- Beatrice loved **Mark Ventmore** (painter; father disowned him). Her letter to Mark miscarried.
- **Colonel Berrington** (brilliant soldier, long leave, quest; was in love with **Mary**). Beatrice asks him for help.
- The **Slave of the Bond / Slave of Silence** (grey-clad, silver-grey lady, brown eyes, grey hair; = **Mary Sartoris/Grey**, Berrington's former fiancée).
- Swiss waiter gives card with Mark's note: "In the little conservatory... Soon as possible." Mark disguised as waiter.

### Chapters III-V: Wedding morning
- Mark tells Beatrice in conservatory; Mark goes to Sir Charles's room; in morning Mark breaks door; Sir Charles found dead, "dead for some hours."
- Richford visits Beatrice with diamonds (Rockmartin gems, £40,000). Richford was seen by Mark too. Doctors Andrews & Oswin.
- Wedding interrupted; Beatrice leaves with Mark. Telegram (grey paper) addressed to Richford found in Sir Charles's room, proving Richford saw body. "Mrs Beacon Light" letter.

### Chapters VI-IX: Richford, Countess
- Beatrice confronts Richford (refuses marriage). Richford attacked by Mark. Richford lunches; salt-bullet on plate (sign of danger).
- Cabbed to 100 Audley Place, Wandsworth; **Carl Sartoris** (cripple, invalid chair, electric machines, flowers) = Mary's brother.
- Lady Rashborough rejects Beatrice. **Countess de la Moray** and **General Gastang** (= Cora & Reggie); seal wax impression on Sir Charles's door; scent drugged Beatrice.
- Body of Sir Charles disappears; hall porter Benwort and night watchman Catton; RPH Rajah suite.

### Chapters X-XVIII: Audley Place & Field
- Inspector **Field**; Macklin (policeman). Berrington & Field infiltrate house; Rajah of Ahbad (= Reggie?); Dr. **Bentwood**; grey lady Mary; Berrington captured; torture by Burmese; Violet Decie (ward of Sir Charles, stage name Adela Vane).
- Field learns Sartoris was Carl Grey, Violet's ex-fiancé, Simla, ruby mines in Burmah.

### Chapters XIX-XXX: Theatre fire, Fleming, Wandsworth
- Field saves Adela Vane at Comedy theatre fire.
- Lawyer George Fleming (Lincoln's Inn Fields): forged deed; stamp 4.4.'93 dated 3 years ago; sold by Acton (law stationer) that morning; £5 note from Wandsworth bank.
- Berrington finds collar marked by Beatrice in the vault under the dining-room floor (Sir Charles's body was there).
- Richford's car crash; Richford dies falling off bridge; Sartoris dies from broken rib.
- Mark's father (wealthy, ruby mines); Sir Charles alive, disguised; Beatrice–Mark engagement; Berrington marries Mary ("Slave of Silence" ends).

### Other
- Publisher's ad pages appended (E. Phillips Oppenheim novels) — ignore.
